Even if you don’t have an elaborate skincare routine, you probably still use lip balm. Chapped lips aren’t just a winter issue—they can happen year-round. Cranking up my personal space heater creates a warm, dry environment that dehydrates my skin and lips, leaving them dry, flaky, and sometimes painful. While drinking water and not licking lips can help, dermatologists say those aren’t the only reasons they get chapped.

Our lips have a unique anatomy. They have thinner skin, low water retention, and fewer oil glands than the rest of our face. That makes them more prone to dryness, says dermatologist Teresa Song, MD.

A good lip balm hydrates, seals in moisture, prevents cracking, and protects the skin barrier from harsh elements, she says. That’s where the ingredients shine and separate good lip balms from great ones. Once you order one of these editor-tested, dermatologist-recommended lip balms, reapplication is key. Dr. Song advises reapplying every two to six hours, and once before bed.

The bottom line: You need something that's going to keep your pout hydrated and supple all year long. Thankfully, we tapped four dermatologists to get their input on what to look for in the best lip balms and which ones they recommend to their clientele. Then, we took matters into our own hands and tested them all ourselves, narrowing down our list to the 11 best lip balms for a wide range of different concerns. Before diving into our list, keep reading to discover what to look for when shopping for your new balm.

While re-evaluating lip balms for this story, I quickly realized I reach for Eadem’s more than any other product in my collection. It checks everything I’m looking for in a lip balm and more. Intensive moisture? Of course. A beautiful glossy sheen? Absolutely. Are there buildable shades and a clear option to match the rest of my makeup? Yup. Dermatologist-tested and endorsed by Dr. Song? You know it.

With each swipe, my lips soak up the nourishing and antioxidant-rich blend of Brazilian açaí and African mongongo butters. Moringa oil provides non-greasy, deep hydration that supports my skin barrier. It also contains a collagen-boosting peptide that smooths the look of my natural lip lines, creating a fuller-looking pout without stinging.

Together, these ingredients keep my lips soft and moisturized for hours. Truthfully, I can go a full day or two without using this balm because the formula is that nourishing. The texture is also impressive—it’s similar to an intense lip mask without the thick, hard-to-spread texture. And it comes in a mess-free tube that tucks away neatly in my Jenni Kayne bag.

But what I love most about this balm is that I no longer need to splurge on a lip scrub and balm. Eadem combines the two products into one. A mix of lactic acid and hibiscus enzymes gently buff away dry, flaky, dead skin cells. By morning, my parched, cracked lips are pillowy soft and smooth again.

As a bonus, it’s available in six colors and a clear option on Amazon. My silver tube of Butter Mochi—a classic clear—is on its last few squeezes and I plan on restocking it, stat. Other gorgeous hues range from seasonal shades, like Boba Bounce, a rich brown, and Bissap Glaze, a deep plum berry to Fig Sauce, a milky rosy brown, and Burnt Malai, a milky desert rose.

Honestly, there isn’t much I don’t love about this lip balm. I talk about Eadem so often that it has become the hot topic of my group chats. Even the Women’s Health and Men’s Health team, including digital designer Taryn Colbert and style editor Joseph Cheatham, have become big fans after my recommendations. “It has the qualities I look for in a lip product which are to keep my lips looking glossy while actually moisturizing them at the same time,” says Colbert.

If I have to nitpick, then it gets a tad goopy when I apply multiple layers. But TBH, that was just for testing purposes, and not a technique I’d use IRL. A thin layer is all I need for soft, glossy lips.

This one is a tried-and-true classic that you can't go wrong with—and it helps that it's a dermatologist-favorite. Dermatologist Divya Shokeen, MD, says the combination of glycerin and shea butter locks in deep hydration and relief from chapped lips. Plus, it's fragrance-free, so you don't have to worry about any unwanted scents.

Fitness editor Cori Ritchey has relied on this classic lip balm for almost a decade. “It's hydrating, not sticky, unscented, and always reliable—truly perfect for every need,” she says. “It’s truly one of the goats.” Our associate health and fitness editor Addison Aloian, is also a long-time Aquaphor fan because it works on chapped lips and peeling skin. “It's my go-to lip product for soft skin that I return to over again,” she says. Another bonus? It doesn't leave stains on her glass cups or water bottles.

While this ointment is unflavored, it does have a petroleum taste, which we're not huge fans of. It's also quite slick and greasy feeling, so you may want to opt for something else if that's not your thing.

I’ve used this lip balm on and off since it launched in 2023. I love its trifecta of lip-smoothing and nourishing ingredients—more on that in a bit—that instantly softens my very dry lips. After a few wears, I only have to swipe on this balm twice a day for long-lasting moisture. My mouth no longer feels dry and cracked, and my lip liners and lipsticks glide on easily when used on top of this product.

With prolonged use—it was my daily go-to for over two years—my lips were consistently smooth, soft, and nourished. Truthfully, I only switch things up because I love trying newness for work reviews and still gift this balm to my parents every birthday and Christmas.

Dr. Song credits the blend of restorative shea butter, moisturizing vitamin B5, and the brand's patented thermal spring water as a win for repairing and soothing damaged lips. The thermal water hails from La Roche-Posay, France (naturally), and contains selenium, an antioxidant-rich mineral.

Despite the richer consistency, this balm melts like butter. It lasts for hours without needing reapplication, and it’s only $10, which is a major plus. Just keep in mind how much product you use—if you squeeze out too much balm, it’ll look ashy. FWIW, La Roche-Posay keeps my lips feeling moisturized and protected year-round.

Ask anyone what their go-to moisturizing lip products are, and you're almost guaranteed to hear this one as a common response—just ask Dr. Shokeen, who tells me it's one of her all-time favorites. It’s packed with a mixture of hyaluronic acid, minerals, and antioxidants that work to mend and revitalize dry, chapped lips, making it perfect for overnight hydration, she says.

This has been in my rotation since 2021 for deep moisture while I snooze. I love how thick and moisturizing the formulation is; my lips feel juicy in the morning. The wearability is also on point—I can swipe on once or twice daily and I’m good to go even in the winter.

Need more proof that Laneige locks in moisture overnight? Colbert fell asleep with it on and woke up facing the fan with lips still soft and moisturized. “It’s perfect after exfoliating and lasts through a night of tossing and turning,” she says.

Laneige is also one of the rare lip masks that includes a tiny spatula for mess-free application. The spatula elevates my selfcare routine and ensures that I scoop the last drop of product before I reorder a replacement.

I personally love all the fun flavors it comes in (there are eight options on Amazon), but if fragrances aren't your thing, you might not love this product as much as I do.

For our annual Skincare Awards package, WH's beauty team tested hundreds of new beauty products. Mogg crowned this new drop her ultimate lip balm because it delivers intense moisture, comes in sheer colors, and has fun packaging.

A blend of zinc, copper, and magnesium hydrates her dry lips and banana juice retains moisture even after she rubs excess product off. It's also infused with coconut and aloe extracts to condition and smooth chapped lips, which earned it a permanent spot in Mogg's daily beauty routine.

Her favorite part about this balm is by far the deliciously sweet scent and fruity flavors. Mogg found the aromas so enticing that she was tempted to eat them. Milk Makeup is available in seven colors, including Quench, a brown beige with a coconut flavor, and Werk Out, a dusty rose that tastes like watermelon.

Associate fitness editor Olivia Luppino is also a fan because it applies smoothly and nourishes her lips. She says it’s also only slightly sticky compared to the other lip balms she tested, such as Aquaphor and Rhode.

Though we fully stand behind this pick, the fruity smell lingers—you should skip it if you don't enjoy sweet scents.

Both Hailey Bieber and her skincare brand, Rhode, have become synonymous with "glazed donut skin," and this moisturizing lip treatment gives my lips that same effect. Most lip glosses leave behind a sticky feel or oily finish, but not Rhode. It provides a super-hydrating feel, with a glossy finish and non-sticky feel. No wonder we crowned it the best lip treatment in our 2023 Beauty Awards. “This one mixes the usual moisturizing suspects like shea butter and natural oils with peptides to plump,” says Underwood.

And we’re not the only fans. Dermatologist Azadeh Shirazi, MD, highlights the combination of nourishing shea butter and collagen-supporting, lip-plumping peptides as standout ingredients. It’s also made with vitamin E, which retains moisture and provides antioxidant protection. Dr. Shirazi likes the rich texture, which helps hydrate and protect dry lips.While the option linked here is the unscented version, you can buy the balm in four additional flavors: strawberry, salted caramel, vanilla, and watermelon. FWIW, Luppino is a big fan of the unscented, untinted version because she prefers a natural look with a glossy finish.I adore Rhode, but Luppino says it’s the thickest and stickiest lip balm, so she doesn’t use it daily. That said, it’s still a nourishing balm with a glossy finish—and it plays nicely with makeup or when layered on its own. And FWIW, I found the tinted versions aren’t grainy. Espresso layered over a pinky-nude lipstick, like my holy grail Charlotte Tilbury Pillow Talk Original, is a stunning combination.

If the word "plumper" scares you, don't worry—BeautyStat doesn't contain menthol, so it won't cause that uncomfortable tingly feeling. Instead, it relies on two peptides to hydrate and plump fine lines for a fuller pout. The volumized look—elimination of lip lines and feathering—lasted up to two hours, and the hydration lingered longer. Most importantly, the results are subtle without painful injections, which is always a win. It just makes your lips look super shiny and, if we do say so ourselves, kissable.

BeautyStat also blends sodium hyaluronate and squalane for extra hydration without feeling heavy or goopy on my lips. Its lightweight texture coats my lips in four colors—ranging from Natural Peach and Baby Pink to my personal favorite Butter Beige, a neutral-pink with a light coat of color. There’s also Mocha, a rich brown that looks gorgeous on both melanin-rich and fair complexions.

It’s also packed with zinc oxide, a mineral SPF that doesn’t leave behind an ashy tint on my lips. It’s also gentle compared to chemical active ingredients, like avobenzone. Not to mention it’s enriched with vitamin C to help repair environmental damage and brighten an uneven skin tone.

Best of all? There’s no off-putting fragrance. Just a light, vanilla-creamsicle scent that adds a welcome touch of summer despite the chilly weather.

Holiday travel is coming up along with fun parties—and I’ll be carrying this slim lip balm in my bag at all-times. I barely need to squeeze the tube for the clear balm to land my fingers and apply it to my lips. I can also apply the balm directly to my mouth and just pat it in and move my lips around a bit to help the product spread. Regardless of application method, it’s quickly become my go-to lip balm for this time of year.

What sets it apart from others on this list is the incredible gel-like balmy texture that melts into my lips. I get a beautiful sheen and my lips feel instantly hydrated and smooth. I genuinely can’t stop smacking my lips because the balm just feels really luxe on my mouth.

I also normally don’t enjoy watermelon scented lip products because the fragrance reminds me of the overly sweet Smackers balm I wore in elementary and middle school. However, Grown Alchemist created the elevated version with this lightly-scented watermelon and vanilla aroma.

Need another reason to shop for this lip balm? At $20 you get 0.4 ounces of product. For comparison, I included Evolvetogether, which sells for $28 and only includes 0.28 ounces of lip balm. Why spend $8 more for a pretty standard natural lip balm, when you could enjoy a more elevated alternative that doesn’t skimp on quality ingredients? Think classic shea butter and rosehip oil for intense hydration. Even with the radiator running, I wake up with softer lips after using Grown Alchemist. Yes, please and thank you!

If you want to go the natural route, I have just the pick for you: Evolvetogether's plant-powered lip balm, which taps coconut oil, shea butter, and jojoba seed oil to coat the lips in a smooth, buttery veil. The best part? There's zero thick or sticky residue left behind. Just the satiny feeling of the natural butters, lavender and chamomile oils. Dr. Song notes the simple and clean formula is effective for light moisture, making it a great fit for anyone who hates the goopy feeling of thicker lip masks or lives somewhere warm year-round.

When Dr. Song says light moisture, she really means it. Colbert likes it for daily wear, but needed to reapply frequently after riding on the back of her friend’s motorcycle for 20 minutes. “When I apply it after my skincare routine I can sit through a few hours of TV and doomscrolling and still have my lips feeling moisturized,” she says.

I love that this balm is available in two different scents—Provence and Anguilla—to suit your mood. I’ve only tried Provence, which is a mix of chamomile, lavender, and vanilla. It smells gorgeous and fresh—never overpowering.Something to note: This formula contains beeswax, so it's not a great option for the vegans out there.

Laneige remains my favorite lip mask, but this one from Ilia is fragrance-free, and only has a light lavender scent from its ingredients, which is great if you have a sensitive nose or skin. I keep this formula in my work tote because I'm not always in the mood for an aroma, but it also never slacks on deep hydration. After applying it nightly for a month, my lips always felt super moisturized and never chapped, which is a huge plus.

“There's nothing worse to me than an artificial fruit taste accidentally getting in my mouth,” says Ritchey. She’s a big fan of this fragrance-free balm and highlights its non-sticky, super moisturizing formula that left her lips feeling brand new after application.

What else makes it a noteworthy inclusion? Ilia combines salicornia, which is a type of flowering plant, with hyaluronic acid to boost hydration and support the skin barrier, says dermatologist Marisa Garshick, MD. It also contains papaya enzymes, which help to get rid of dead skin cells. Due to the fruit's exfoliating properties, you should only use this twice daily to avoid overscrubbing your lips.

The only downside with this lip mask is that it comes in a pot instead of a squeezable tube, so it’s not as clean when applying. For Ritchey and her longer nails that’s a minor problem. “It's difficult to get the product out of the container, especially when it's towards the bottom,” she says. “However, the product is good enough that it's worth living with the difficult container!” If you’re also sporting longer nails, this balm easily applies with a cotton bud. And since it’s clear, don’t be surprised if your partner tries to swipe this one from your medicine cabinet. Yup, it’s that good.

This Women's Health Skincare Award-winning balm features a piña colada–esque flavor that brings a tropical touch to Underwood’s mornings. But most importantly, it’s an untinted SPF lip balm that doesn’t have the unpleasant sunscreen taste. We like to wear it on its own each morning for the most natural appearance.

We're also impressed by the epic lineup of nourishing ingredients, like lanolin. Research shows that lanolin can reduce transepidermal water loss (TEWL) by up to 30%, ensuring our lips are amply moisturized. However, lanolin can irritate some people, according to the American Academy of Dermatology. While that hasn’t been Underwood’s experience, if that happens to you, it’s best to stop using this one.

Still, the thicker formula is also infused with a plethora of castor seed oil, beeswax, shea butter, grapeseed oil, vitamin E, and coconut oil. This broad-spectrum sunscreen combines four types of active chemical ingredients that provide SPF 30 coverage that avoids a white cast.

Another limitation to this balm? We need a separate lip balm for nighttime—wearing SPF to bed doesn't make sense since we’re not exposed to harmful ultraviolet rays while we slumber.

Dr. Song name-checked three types of ingredients to watch for—humectants, emollients, and occlusives—and shared how they keep the lips hydrated, smooth, and protected.

You’ll want to stay away from alcohol, which causes excessive dryness. Mineral oil may clog pores around the lips, and strong fragrances can lead to irritation and rashes. Though menthol, camphor, and phenol have a cooling sensation, they will irritate and dry the lips over time.

Dr. Song also recommends swapping out lip balms when seasons change and when you're traveling to a different climate. Use lighter formulas such as Rhode’s Peptide Lip Treatment in warm or humid climates and thicker formulas like the Laneige Lip Mask in cold or dry weather.

To find the best lip balms, I reevaluated my massive collection of products. I considered their ingredients and consistency, as well as their functional and cosmetic benefits. For example, I evaluated how long the hydration lasted and how sticky each swipe felt.

While my favorites range from $5 to $30, I didn’t notice a decline in the quality or feel of more affordable lip balms, nor did pricier picks equate to dramatic hydration.

Additionally, I ensured there was a mix of lightweight formulas for daily wear and heavier balms for overnight use. Because I love experimenting with my lipstick and lip liner combos, I awarded bonus points to balms that come in a variety of tints. I also factored in how vibrant or sheer each hue was on its own and how they layered with makeup. There are clear options for anyone who prefers a more natural look.

To further refine the list, I asked four dermatologists about their go-to picks. I also recruited other WH staffers: beauty director Brian Underwood, beauty editorial assistant Katie Mogg, and associate health and wellness editor Addison Aloian. Beauty contributors Lily Wohlner and Danielle Jackson joined as testers for this story.

When we initially published this story in February 2024, we featured 20 lip balms. For our latest 2026 update, we tried 40 lip balms over a year and settled on 10 tried-and-true recommendations that we’re actually using this fall and beyond. They're all aligned with dermatological guidance and nourish our lips for hours.

In a recent post on social media, Dogecoin engineer Michi Lumin noted that a GitHub billing issue affecting Dogecoin Core has been addressed, although uncertainty remains on how the expenses will be handled in the coming months.

Lumin disclosed that Dogecoin Core's GitHub account ran into billing issues, which she resolved by personally paying the arrears and then switching the billing to herself.

This situation follows major Dogecoin Core developer Patrick Lodder's absence on the 'core' front, with Lumin describing him as missing in action (MIA). However, Lumin clarified that this reflected her own personal experience and speculated that others might have remained in contact with him.

"So @dogecoin , Pat Lodder has gone MIA for months on the Core front (at least to ME. If others have talked to him, great!), and the Core GitHub has run into some billing issues. I've paid the arrears personally and switched billing to myself," Lumin wrote.

@Doge_France @dogecoin as far as i know it was fees for CI workers or actions that they bill/meter. I've been reachable but that's a whole other kettle of bees around here. Either way, it's paid right now, so we'll see how next month goes and i'll address it then if i need to.

The update from Lumin prompted a response from Dogecoin community member 'Doge France', who offered to contribute financially if assistance was needed, saying that keeping the Core GitHub infrastructure operational should be a priority.

Responding to the offer, Lumin explained that the outstanding charges appeared to be related to GitHub Actions or continuous integration (CI) workers, whose usage is billed according to consumption.

Although the immediate payment has been completed, Lumin stopped short of confirming a long-term funding arrangement for the Core GitHub. The developer said the next billing cycle would provide a clearer picture, which will be addressed if necessary.

"As far as i know, it was fees for CI workers or actions that they bill/meter.  I've been reachable but that's a whole other kettle of bees around here. Either way, it's paid right now, so we'll see how next month goes and i'll address it then if i need to," Lumin wrote.

The Dogecoin Foundation, a non-profit organization for which Lumin serves as principal engineer, supports open-source development, advocacy, and community work for Dogecoin and relies primarily on community contributions for its funding.

In the past month, Dogecoin announced a consolidation across its ecosystem with the launch of Dogecoin Labs, which unites Dogecoin’s product teams, technology and applications.

#5248. Bank of America Warns of 50 bps Fed Hike in December: Is Bitcoin Heading for Another 2022-Style Drop?

Bank of America (BofA) says hot CPI puts a 50bps December Fed hike on the table. BTC fell a week later after 5 of the last 6 big hikes.

Bank of America said this week that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates by half a percentage point in December. The warning came after Tuesday’s October inflation report ran hotter than expected for a third month in a row. In Bitcoin news, the coin trades at $73,888 on Binance, down 0.6% in 24 hours. It dropped to $72,727 on Tuesday after the report, its lowest price since August 20.

The bank still expects the Fed to raise rates by 0.25 percentage points, or 25 basis points (bps), at its December 8–9 meeting. But it says the case for a bigger move is growing, and it calls the Fed’s decision to hold rates in October a possible policy mistake.

Traders are starting to listen. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 50 bps or more in December rose from 0.6% on Monday to 11.4% on Wednesday.

BANK OF AMERICA WARNS FED COULD DELIVER 50BPS HIKE IN DECEMBER

Bank of America says October's hot CPI report virtually guarantees a December Fed rate hike — and opens the door to a larger 50bps move.

Headline CPI rose 0.4%, while core CPI climbed 0.3%, marking a third…

— *Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaone) November 11, 2026

The bank’s call rests on three months of hot data. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, and core prices, which leave out food and energy because they swing the most, rose 0.3%. Both beat forecasts, the third upside surprise in a row in the Bureau of Labor Statistics report.

Bank of America now estimates that core PCE inflation, the Fed’s preferred measure, is running at 3.3% a year. The Fed’s target is 2%. The bank says price rises are spreading from goods to services, with electronics, airfares and hotels leading the increases.

Its base case is still a 25 bps hike in December. The change is in the risks: a 50 bps move is now possible, and the bank sees a growing chance of another hike in January instead of March.

The bank is not alone. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech on Tuesday morning that he leans toward a 25 bps hike in December. If core inflation came in around 0.3% again, he said, a 50 bps hike “should be considered.” It did.

Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more. That tends to pull money out of risky assets like BTC, and a faster pace of hikes pulls harder.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

The size of the hike has mattered for BTC. We measured Bitcoin’s price on Binance from the 2 p.m. ET announcement of each Fed rate hike since 2022 to one week later. That covers 12 hikes: six of 50 bps or more and six of 25 bps.

After the six big hikes, BTC was lower a week later five times. The median move was a 6% drop. The worst came after the 50 bps hike in May 2022, when BTC fell 23% in a week.

After the six 25 bps hikes, the picture was milder. BTC was lower a week later four times, but the median move was a drop of just 0.6%.

The record comes with a caveat. All six big hikes happened in 2022, a bear market that also saw the collapses of Terra in May and FTX in November. Those crashes made the falls after the May and November hikes worse.

The most recent hike was a 25 bps move on September 16. BTC rose 11.3% in the week after it, as the uncertainty that had built up before the meeting cleared. That makes the size of December’s hike, more than the hike itself, the Bitcoin news to watch.

#5245. Bitcoin Crash Coming? Analyst Revisits 2014, 2018, and 2022 Pattern Ahead Of Midterm Elections

Bitcoin (BTC) could face another significant correction as the November 3 U.S. midterm elections approach, with analysts pointing to a historical pattern that has coincided with major BTC price declines during previous election cycles.

With the 2026 midterm elections just days away, market observers are examining Bitcoin’s performance around the 2014, 2018, and 2022 elections to see whether another downturn is approaching.

Although the historical similarities do not establish that elections directly influence cryptocurrency prices, the repeated appearance of major corrections during these periods has raised questions about Bitcoin’s near-term direction.

According to crypto analytics platform Alphractal, Bitcoin was already experiencing bearish conditions before each of the previous three midterm elections. However, selling pressure continued after Election Day, with the cryptocurrency eventually reaching significant cycle lows.

Looking back at the 2014 U.S. midterm elections held on November 4, Bitcoin was already caught in an extended bear market. The cryptocurrency continued declining in the weeks that followed, eventually reaching its cycle bottom in January 2015.

A similar development occurred in 2018. Bitcoin was trading around $6,400 when Americans headed to the polls on November 6. Although the market initially experienced a period of relative stability, BTC subsequently suffered a sharp decline, losing approximately 40% over the following month before establishing its cycle bottom in December.

Meanwhile, during the 2022 election cycle, Bitcoin had already experienced considerable losses by the time the November 8 elections took place. The collapse of cryptocurrency exchange FTX occurred around the same period, triggering another wave of selling that pushed BTC toward $15,500 and marked the bottom of that market cycle.

According to Alphractal, these three occurrences raise an interesting question about whether Bitcoin’s performance has any meaningful relationship with the U.S. electoral calendar.

The analytics platform emphasized that Bitcoin was already in a bear market ahead of all three elections. Consequently, the subsequent declines could have reflected broader cryptocurrency market conditions and the asset’s four-year cycle rather than the elections themselves.

Additionally, popular analyst Ali Martinez highlighted Bitcoin’s historical performance across four U.S. midterm election cycles.

According to Martinez, BTC recorded significant declines around the 2010, 2014, 2018, and 2022 midterm elections, with reported losses of 72%, 65%, 52%, and 27%, respectively.

The analyst considers this repeated downside performance a pattern worth monitoring as another election approaches on November 3.

Furthermore, Martinez pointed to Bitcoin’s fourth-quarter returns during previous midterm election years. His figures show that BTC gained 391% in the fourth quarter of 2010, while the cryptocurrency recorded losses of 16.70% in 2014, 42.16% in 2018, and 14.75% in 2022.

The figures suggest that three of the four election-year fourth quarters ended negatively. However, the 2010 rally stands out as an exception, particularly because Bitcoin was still in its early stages of development.

For the upcoming election, Martinez identified $73,000 as an important price level to watch. He pointed to Bitcoin’s short-term holder cost basis, which represents the average acquisition price of coins held by relatively recent market participants.

According to his assessment, this level could become an important support area if selling pressure increases following the elections. A recovery from that region would potentially strengthen the bullish outlook, while continued weakness could signal further deterioration in market conditions.

Beyond the historical election pattern, technical analyst Crypto Patel has also raised concerns about Bitcoin’s immediate price direction, suggesting another substantial decline is possible.

In a recent market update, the pundit said Bitcoin had already fallen about 12% from his previously identified short-entry area. He explained that his bearish outlook originated from technical chart analysis rather than negative headlines or developments affecting the cryptocurrency industry.

The analyst based his assessment on Smart Money Concepts (SMC), which examines market structure, liquidity movements, and price action to identify potential trading opportunities.

Notably, Patel explained that Bitcoin’s price structure had produced a higher high, leading him to anticipate a subsequent move toward a higher low. He also highlighted the removal of inducement liquidity and a higher-timeframe candle closing below the relevant inducement level as additional bearish signals.

Regarding his latest projections, he identified $66,000 to $62,000 as his potential downside target, provided Bitcoin remains below $81,950.

However, the analyst also established a level that would invalidate his short-term bearish outlook. According to Patel, a higher-timeframe candle closing above $84,870 would prompt him to reconsider his position and return to a bullish stance, with expectations of a move beyond $100,000.

These projections suggest that Bitcoin could experience additional volatility as traders assess the market’s technical structure alongside the approaching U.S. elections.

At press time, BTC was trading at $71,454, down 3.92% over the past 24 hours.

#5244. The ‘Midlife Crisis’ Isn’t Real. The Actual Risk Is Believing the Myth.

Knowing the reality can benefit your physical and mental health.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

If you ask someone what comes to mind when they hear the word midlife, 99.9 percent of the time the answer will be very specific: crisis. Ideas about middle age tend to skew negative, no matter the cause.

As a midlife researcher, this is worrying to me because I know just how pernicious these legacy beliefs can be. Yet the most prevalent negative interpretations of midlife are not supported by the research. The truth is so much more hopeful and, frankly, interesting.

While it’s hard to predict exactly who will experience this, it’s likely that 10 to 20 percent of people in midlife will go through some intense period of challenge and growth. For those folks, it’s important to remember that this isn’t a bad thing. First of all, the “crisis” is only part of the story, and not even the most interesting part. Whatever challenges you face are likely to be followed by changes to your life that will help you become freer, stronger, and more tuned in to what you really want for yourself in the second half of your life.

Debunking the myth of the midlife crisis isn’t just about correcting the record—it’s about harm reduction. Cultural notions have a real-time effect on our perception of our health and well-being in our middle years, and if the “information” is more myth than reality, that can have negative effects on our physical, psychological, and cognitive health.

Research done by Becca Levy, PhD, a professor of public health and psychology at Yale, and summarized in her book Breaking the Age Code, has shown the power of both negative and positive beliefs about aging to impact our healthspan and lifespan. Levy found that those who had more positive images of aging (e.g., being healthy and active) lived longer than those with the more stereotypical views about older adults as weak, forgetful, and slow. She also found that those with a more positive mindset about aging were healthier, with lower blood pressure and a lower risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease.

Beliefs about aging can eclipse the truth in many arenas. If a woman in her 50s whose children have just left the nest goes to see her physician about feeling excessively fatigued, depressed, and sleepless, the cliché of the midlife crisis makes it more likely that her concerns will be dismissed. This can lead to misdiagnosis for more serious conditions such as depression, autoimmune disorders, or hormonal deficiencies, which if recognized can be treated properly.

One of the best ways to set ourselves up for success when the sea of life starts to get choppy is to pay close attention to the way we are thinking about our story. Whether we know it or not, we are always telling ourselves stories in order to make meaning out of what happens to us and how it makes us feel. When we’re going through a rough patch, it helps immensely to take control of the narrative—moving from a negative frame of mind to a more hopeful one that emphasizes agency and opportunity. On the opposite end of the spectrum from folks who enter midlife ready for battle, many enter midlife on autopilot. Some assume they are stuck with the decisions made early in adulthood. Others want out but don’t imagine the alternatives or can’t see ways to improve circumstances.

Either way, it’s important to remember that it is possible to make tweaks or small changes in midlife; they don’t have to be radical ones. One of my colleagues on the MacArthur Foundation Research Network on Successful Midlife Development used to say, “Some people are so fed up at work that they quit their jobs in frustration, when all they really needed was a two-week vacation.” When we sleepwalk through midlife, at best it’s a missed opportunity for growth, and at worst it simply delays the challenges that will inevitably surface. What we know from the research is that middle age—whether or not you go through a “crisis”—is the time to reflect and make change.

I like to think of midlife as halftime in sports: Some of the important plays have been made, but not all. While a little discomfort with the poor choices of our past isn’t a bad thing, getting mired in regret isn’t something that helps anybody. You have the opportunity to breathe, examine what has come before, and start analyzing what you need to do next to reach your goals or modify them. There is plenty of time left after midlife, so reflection can help people see how they might move in different directions.

For those who don’t know where to begin when it comes to reflecting on their life story and even changing it, there is good research to suggest that a “life review” can help. When done well, a midlife review can help you make sense of the past and bring clarity to your goals moving forward (find out more about how to do it below).

One strategy is to do life reviews at the decade milestones (40, 50, 60) and possibly at the halfway marks (45, 55, 65). Another strategy is to do it when there are significant life events that might require some readjustments, such as going through a divorce, a job loss, or having a child leave home. Midlife is a great time to revisit old stories and even consider some rewrites and new beginnings.

It is important to keep in mind that it is unlikely that you will have accomplished everything you expected to by age 40, 50, or even 60. And it is unrealistic to think you will be happy with all areas of your life. If you think you are having a midlife crisis, ask yourself whether it’s really a crisis or if it’s just that you’re not happy with how some things are going. Maybe it’s just a time to make some changes. The life-shattering, ego-dissembling portrayal of the inescapable midlife crisis we have all become accustomed to is neither inevitable nor universal.

#5241. Bitcoin Core Breaks Silence on Three Patched Security Vulnerabilities

Bitcoin Core developers have revealed three key security vulnerabilities, including a high-severity flaw that could potentially disrupt the mining capabilities of the Bitcoin network, preventing miners from creating new blocks.

As revealed in security advisories published on Nov. 10, the vulnerabilities impacted various elements of the Bitcoin Core software that powers many nodes underpinning the world's leading cryptocurrency.

One of the vulnerabilities, titled CVE-2025-62861, was rated as a high-severity issue due to its potential effect on Bitcoin miners.

The bug has the potential to create problems after a blockchain reorganization, which is when previously accepted blocks are replaced by the network with an alternative chain.

More precisely, the issue could cause an inconsistent state in the node's mempool, where all unconfirmed transactions are stored.

The vulnerability impacted Bitcoin Core software versions 28.0-28.2 and 29.0-29.1.

It was first reported on Sept. 26, 2025, by security researcher Niklas Goegge.

Beyond the mining vulnerability, Bitcoin Core developers have announced two further security problems, rated medium severity.

The first one (CVE-2025-62859) could enable malicious network participants to slow down Bitcoin block processing through an exploit that involves changes in transaction witness data.

Under some circumstances, it could make an affected node wait for up to 10 minutes before processing a block.

Moreover, such an attack could be repeated indefinitely on the node when the latter is running in specific configurations.

The vulnerability was found by Eugene Siegel in April 2025.

The second vulnerability (CVE-2025-62860) involved Bitcoin nodes that operate on the anonymous Tor network.

In fact, the Bitcoin Core developers revealed that thousands of reachable Bitcoin mainnet nodes had been granting permissions for incoming Tor connections.

Nevertheless, the issue did not affect nodes that do not use the optional whitelist configuration.

The three vulnerabilities are not new discoveries.

In fact, all of the issues were already fixed by the Bitcoin Core developers in October 2025.

The fixes were integrated into both Bitcoin Core 30.0, which was released on Oct. 10, and Bitcoin Core 29.2, rolled out on Oct. 14.

The high-severity mining vulnerability was also patched in Bitcoin Core 28.3.

The delay in the disclosure of the vulnerabilities was in line with the Bitcoin Core security policy, which usually calls for developers to wait at least two weeks after the end of life of the last affected software version before publishing details of medium- or high-severity vulnerabilities.

#5240. The 7 Best Firming Body Lotions for Tightening Skin, Tested by Experts

Editors gave top marks to formulas from Nivea and Charlotte Tilbury.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Skin changes are part of life—thanks to sun exposure, the natural dip in collagen and elastin once you hit your late 20s, or shifts in weight (hi, pregnancy!). So if your skin doesn’t quite have the same snap-back it once did, that’s completely normal. The good news? You don’t need pricey lasers or an intense 10-step routine to see a difference. The right body-firming lotion can help skin look plumper, smoother, and more resilient.

Firming body lotions can offer smoother, tighter, and less dimpled skin. While nothing can compare to the results you may get from an in-office procedure—topicals aren’t going to work miracles, after all—you might be surprised at just how far hydration can improve the appearance of crepey skin. “The physical transformation of hydration can be profound on our skin,” says dermatologist Nava Greenfield, MD. “The skin will actually appear plumper when a lotion used to ‘firm’ is applied. Adding nutrients to the skin on a consistent basis can also help in creating a healthy, firm appearance.”

Like other categories of skincare products, some firming formulas will always be better than others. To help streamline your shopping experience, I asked dermatologists for their expertise on how to shop for body lotions, along with product recommendations.

For the past few months, beauty contributor Danielle Blundell and I have been researching and testing the best firming lotions. After consulting six dermatologists for their shopping guidance, we asked for their no-fail recommendations as a starting point. We got our hands on some of these picks and shared our testing feedback to help you determine which option works for your unique beauty needs. And to ensure there was a variety of firming body lotions across all budgets, we spent hundreds of hours vetting products for their ingredient list, formulation, absorbency, long- and short-term hydration and firming benefits, and pricing. Of the dozens we tested, these were the best ones we’re willing to auto-refill.

So, get ready for smoother, tighter, and, yes, firmer skin.

Given the fast-acting results Blundell experienced, and the impressive ingredient list we knew the Nivea Skin Toning Gel-Cream was our best overall option. When looking at price, packaging size, and the strength of a given formula’s ingredients, this lightweight cream is hard to beat.

The combination of antioxidant Coenzyme Q10, which aids in cell turnover, and L-carnitine, a chemical known to bolster skin energy reserves and oxygen consumption in skin cells, packs a firming and hydrating punch that’ll leave your skin feeling silky-smooth. We saw improved tightness in just two weeks with twice daily use, and you can choose between almond and lotus scents depending on your preferences for fragrances.

Blundell loves the gel-like texture of this one—it’s a little bit runny right out of the tube, but it sinks into her skin with minimal rubbing and goes on with a bit of a cooling sensation, which feels especially refreshing in the mornings before work and during any waterfront vacations you’re taking. Hours after a quick application (and even a SoulCycle class and quick shower later), Blundell’s legs looked slightly more taut and still felt supple to the touch, as though she had just put the lotion on.

Sometimes the best products are the ones you’ll use religiously. To that end, you can slather on this lotion morning, noon, and night, thanks to its under $10 price tag and light-but-creamy texture that’s easy to apply. Blundell saw results like immediate hydration, but it took three weeks to notice less crepey skin.

“Although the role of topical collagen isn't fully understood yet, this product contains a hydrating form of vitamin B3, niacinamide, and a form of B5 panthenol, which strengthen skin and improve skin quality,” says Dr. Nazarian. “It also absorbs really nicely and applies easily and quickly, making it a great and affordable option for improving skin health.”

Dr. Sartor mentions the lotion does include a nice mix of moisturizers (petrolatum, stearic acid) to prevent water loss as well as antioxidants (niacinamide, tocopheryl acetate) for firming benefits, especially for its cost. “It also contains free fatty acids (palmitic acid) to repair the skin barrier,” she adds.

The only downside for the price? The formula contains a synthetic fragrance, so if you have sensitive skin, you might want to skip it for that reason.

Why settle for just skin firming on your body when you enjoy it on your face as well? This 2-in-1 lotion earned major snaps from dermatologist Dr. Lauren Penzi, MD, for that reason. "It has a powerful retinol and peptide complex that exfoliates to support the skin's renewal process," she says. That means it’ll go to work on discoloration and fine lines on your face and body while you sleep, since it’s a night treatment.

She highlights the intensive humectant and emollient moisturizers and vitamins that keep the skin hydrated for 24 hours as essential for skin firming and smoothing. You can see that in the texture; it’s rich and thick but still rubs in easily and dries quickly, so it’s not a pain to put on before bed.

A great place to give it a go first might be the neck and chest, where wrinkles tend to start popping up sooner than we all might like. Just keep in mind your skin type. Women with oily or combination skin might find it a tad heavy, so start with a pea-sized amount on the face and only add more as needed. Those with normal or dry skin will love this one due to its wonderfully hydrating formula.

Although Revision is a pricey pick, Dr. Nazarian argues it’s well worth the splurge because of the science-backed results and clinical trials. “It combines a cocktail of peptides and antioxidants to promote collagen, prevent breakdown, and ingredients like glucosamine to support cell turnover.” In other words, this product will help tighten loose skin.

BodiContour can be used before and after professional treatments to help enhance your results. However, you should wait until any broken skin is fully healed after your procedure before incorporating this cream back into your routine.

Dr. Sartor likes the hyaluronic acid in the formula as well but notes that the lotion is part of a three-step regimen. She thinks the brand’s promised results—from the fading of sun damage to the tightening of dimply, saggy skin—will be seen with use of the entire system. And even if a little lotion does go a long way, the instructions do recommend applying it twice a day and exfoliating twice a week. So with that does come a significant investment of time and money.

It's not called Magic Cream for nothing. This silky body cream blends caffeine and hydrating all-star hyaluronic acid to smooth and firm the skin. "It also includes the iconic magic 8 matrix, which includes vitamin C and E, aloe vera, camellia oil, rosehip oil, and shea butter, plus moisturizing frangipani flower extract," says dermatologist Dr. Marisa Garshick, MD. "Together this helps to brighten the skin and leave the skin glowing."

Of all the formulas Blundell tried, the Magic Body Cream is the one that left the most noticeable sheen and slight blurring effect on her skin. Putting it on feels luxurious, too; it’s rich but not so heavy that it doesn’t blend well, and it has a similar fragrance to its sister product, Magic Cream anti-aging face moisturizer. The only downside? At $65 a pop, it’s expensive, so Blundell saves it for nights when she’s showing a little skin or wants to target visible areas like the arms, legs, and tummy when sporting resort wear.

StriVectin is well regarded as a top-tier line for anti-aging and skin-firming products, and this rich body cream is a shining example of why the brand has a cult-like following among beauty insiders. And it all starts with the ingredients. A combination of turmeric root and jojoba seed extracts paired with a buttery blend of shea, murumuru, and cupuacu provide deep moisture to improve the look of skin texture and crepiness, says dermatologist Brendan Camp, MD. The turmeric helps brighten uneven skin tone while peptides and jojoba seed extract work together to tighten the skin and make it appear visibly more firm.

If you’re looking to fight back against particularly crepey arms or kneecaps, Dr. Sartor points out that this formula does include more antioxidants than some of the less expensive drugstore options. She also highlights the caffeine and collagen peptides, which work in tandem with the other firming extracts mentioned above. “This would be a good option for more mature skin in need of a richer moisturizer with more skin benefits,” she says.Although spending $44 might seem like a lot, there are other luxury anti-aging lotions out there selling for $165 to $220. If it helps, each container will last around 6 to 12 weeks, depending on how often you apply and if you’re slathering all over or just targeting a smaller area of your body. Regardless, even if you buy a few replacements in the year at $176, you get a year’s worth of product for significantly less than if you were splurging on a single high-end firming body lotion.

If you’re looking for an ultralight, gel-like product that can smooth, plump, and deliver silky-to-the-touch skin, then Nécessaire The Body Serum is the best pick for you. The formula is made with gentle clean ingredients that don’t skimp on quality. It combines ceramides with five molecular weights of hyaluronic acid which provides multilevel hydration. The result: a plumping finish that delivers a bit of lift and tautness. Glycerin further moisturizes the skin, while aloe vera calms redness and irritation. There’s also niacinamide for fine line-fighting benefits.

I’ve been using this serum on and off for a few years, and I can confidently attest to its effectiveness. It helps clear up eczema flare-ups, and has been a beauty lifesaver during the winter when it’s freezing outdoors and my radiator is cranked up inside. A single layer of the clear serum soaks into my skin in seconds, and if your skin is extra parched like mine is then you can apply additional layers as needed without pilling or leaving behind a sticky mess. It’s a year-round must-have for me because in the spring and summer I can just get away with using this instead of a thick lotion or cream.

“This serum does not have any firming ingredients but instead contains hyaluronic acid to plump skin appearance and ceramides to repair the skin barrier,” says Dr. Sartor. “This serum also contains lecithin to help prevent further water loss from the skin surface.”

Honestly, the only downside with this serum is that it’s fragrance-free. Nécessaire does fragrances so incredibly well that I wish they extended their enticing aromas into The Body Serum as well. Still, I fully stand by this serum and if you’re on the fence give it a go and see for yourself. With Amazon Prime’s signature two-day shipping and a 30-day money-back guarantee you have extra reassurance to treat yourself.

You’ve probably been using body lotion since middle school, and firming formulas look and feel roughly the same. They’re applied the same way, too; just massage a dollop into the skin, let it dry for a bit, and you’re good to go on with your day. A few key features, though, are what can separate a good option from a great one, and this is what you’ll want to consider when shopping for the best firming body lotions.

For dermatologist Dr. Rachel Nazarian, MD, certain ingredients are a must if you’re looking to tone and improve the skin’s texture.

Ultimately, whatever lotion, oil, serum, or cream you choose comes down to your skin’s needs. On the most basic level, sometimes it’s just a matter of texture preference—maybe you like the lightness of an oil or serum and want to go that route, or the richness of a cream is what you gravitate toward in the colder months. But some skin types really do fare better with certain formats over others, so you’ll want to keep that in mind.

Serums, gels, and lotions are lightweight and generally better suited for women under 40 with normal or acne-prone skin. Because they’re not heavy, they’re also fantastic if you have sensitive skin all over. You can follow it up with a cream as spot treatment in areas like your kneecaps and elbows that require more moisturization, says Dr. Sartor.

Creams are thick and deeply hydrating, making them helpful for dry and mature skin. You can also use them if you have sensitive skin. However, there is a trade-off. Hyaluronic acid penetrates the skin more easily in lighter serums and gels, so you might need to choose between a gentler product and a more effective moisturizer.

Though not as important as ingredients or format, size can matter when it comes to choosing a firming body lotion, mainly because it can factor into a product’s price and usage. If you want to make a smaller, more expensive lotion go further, consider applying it to target areas—think the butt, thighs, tummy, or upper arms. Consistency is key, though, so a product that you can use more frequently could be better than something you’d have to use sparingly.

Dr. Nava Greenfield, MD, is a board-certified dermatologist at Schweiger Dermatology Group in New York City.

Dr. Rachel Nazarian MD, FAAD, is a board-certified dermatologist with Schweiger Dermatology Group in New York City.

Dr. Quynh-Giao Sartor, MD, FAAD, is a board-certified dermatologist at Westlake Dermatology in Houston, Texas.

Dr. Lauren Penzi, MD, is a board-certified dermatologist at MDCS Dermatology: Medical Dermatology & Cosmetic Surgery in New York.

Dr. Marisa Garshick, MD, FAAD, is a board-certified dermatologist and assistant clinical professor of dermatology at Cornell - New York Presbyterian Medical Center.

Dr. Brendan Camp, MD, FAAD, is a board-certified dermatologist at MDCS Dermatology in New York.

It’s important to manage your expectations for firming lotions—they’re not the cure-all for sagging skin. Severe laxity and deep folds aren’t going to disappear overnight, but your skin will perk up and even plump a bit temporarily upon application.

“You can expect to see your skin slowly showing fewer fine lines and less sag,” says Dr. Greenfield. “A firming cream also has the potential to introduce nutrients that allow your skin to feel smoother and more supple.”

Proper timing is key for absorption and even application, so do yourself a favor and apply right after you’ve just bathed so it sinks in easily, especially if you’re only using this kind of product once a day.

“It is best to apply body lotion when your skin is still damp from a shower but not wet,” says Dr. Greenfield. “Towel dried is optimal. After exfoliating, it is crucial to apply a moisturizer. Best results will ultimately be with consistent and liberal use.”

“Creams are not capable of the same type of tightening that lasers and surgical options can offer,” says Dr. Nazarian. “Despite this, with consistent, continued use, you can certainly see improvement in laxity over time.” But again, commitment to regular use will impact results because everyone’s skin is fighting an uphill battle to a certain extent, at least when it comes to the loss of skin firmness and volume. For the best results, you have to commit to using one regularly to improve the quality of skin laxity, says Dr. Nazarian.

The short answer is yes—but with the caveat that it’s possible to have some kind of a reaction to any body lotion or cream. “Most of these body firming lotions have very little risk,” says Dr. Nazarian. “They are often directed to be used daily, some even twice a day. Major risks include irritation from one of the ingredients or a potential allergy to one of the ingredients.”

Just steer clear of anything with retinol in it, if you’re nursing or pregnant, and discontinue use of a product you have a negative reaction to. “Occasionally, people may experience drying of their skin, especially if the ingredients have the ability to decrease oil production, such as with retinol,” says Dr. Nazarian. “Monitor for those changes and decrease use if they are noted.”

Additional reporting by Danielle Blundell.

#5239. Ripple-Backed Evernorth Plunges 40% as Insiders Move to Sell 73.7 Million Shares

Ripple-backed XRP treasury company Evernorth Holdings (XRPN) is under extreme pressure as its shares have declined by over 40% while big investors like Ripple Labs move closer to potentially selling millions of shares.

Earlier this week, Evernorth filed a prospectus with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), indicating that the XRP-focused company has registered a whopping 73,688,162 Class A shares for potential resale by existing shareholders.

Evernorth's prospectus comes as the XRP-focused company is enduring a brutal stock market debut. XRPN began trading on Nasdaq on Oct. 12.

On Nov. 10, Evernorth's stock price dropped 23.54%. XRPN ended the day at $7.96, compared to $10.41 in the previous trading session. Moreover, about 1.39 million shares were traded, which is a significant jump from about 369,000 shares on Nov. 9.

So far, Evernorth's share price has declined by around 48% from its closing price on Oct. 28 ($15.26). The magnitude of the decline is even greater if we consider the high share price on its debut day ($19.39). XRPN's stock price is down by around 59% from that high.

Some of the biggest names and companies linked to the XRP ecosystem are shareholders who have registered shares for potential sale, as per the prospectus filed with the SEC.

For instance, the biggest shareholder is Arrington XRP Capital Fund, which was a sponsor of the merger between Evernorth and Armada Acquisition Corp. II. It has about 33.82 million shares registered for possible resale.

Similarly, the second-largest shareholder is Ripple Labs, which has about 18.14 million shares registered. Then there are various entities linked to SBI Holdings, a big Japanese financial institution. They have 11.79 million shares registered, as per the prospectus filed with the SEC.

The Larsen Lam Children's Remainder Trust, which is linked to Ripple co-founder Chris Larsen, has about 7.15 million shares registered for possible sale.

Other names mentioned in the filing include Pantera Capital, GSR Markets Switzerland and Kraken parent firm Payward.

It is important to understand that the fact that they've registered shares for sale doesn't mean that these investors have sold their holdings or necessarily plan to sell them.

For example, Ripple, the Arrington-sponsored entity and a Larsen-linked entity are all subject to six-month lock-up agreements following the completion of Evernorth's business combination on Oct. 9.

These lock-up agreements are typically set to expire on April 9, 2027, with some exceptions.

BTC slips as Nvidia sinks 9% after hours and MSCI drops Strategy. ETFs lost $1.88B in November, 94% of it from IBIT.

In Bitcoin news, the coin fell from $74,811 to $73,480 within two hours of the U.S. close. Bitcoin slipped overnight after two shocks hit U.S. markets after Wednesday’s close. Nvidia shares fell about 9% in after-hours trading on a new report about CEO Jensen Huang. Index provider MSCI also confirmed it will remove Strategy, the largest corporate Bitcoin holder, from its global indexes.

It trades at $73,588 on Binance on Thursday morning, down 0.4% in 24 hours and 5.8% in a week.

The funds are not helping. U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) lost $299.8 million on Wednesday, their fifth straight day of outflows. Nasdaq futures are down 0.9%.

Bitcoin ETFs Shed $300 Million, Ether Funds Lose $145 Million

According to SoSoValue, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $300 million in net outflows on November 11, while Morgan Stanley's MSBT led individual fund inflows with $8.96 million. Spot Ethereum ETFs saw $145 million in… pic.twitter.com/5sn88B2JQX

— Wu Blockchain (@WuBlockchain) November 12, 2026

So what happened, and how much of the selling comes from the ETFs?

The first hit came from Nvidia, the world’s most valuable chipmaker. The New York Times reported on Wednesday evening that Huang had a second relationship with a senior employee who reports to him. The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to remove him as CEO.

Nvidia had closed the day up 2.9% at $173.73. Within two hours, it traded at $157.99, down 9.1%. It is still down 8.6% before Thursday’s open. Nvidia has lost about 15% since last Friday. It first fell on Monday, after its board opened a separate probe into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

Bitcoin has traded closely with tech stocks this year, and it fell with them. Nasdaq 100 futures dropped 1.1% in the same two hours.

The second hit is closer to crypto. MSCI, whose indexes guide trillions of dollars in index funds, will delete Strategy from its global indexes after the market close on November 30. It ruled that Strategy looks more like an investment fund holding Bitcoin than an operating business. Japan’s Metaplanet and Upexi are also being removed.

Funds that track those indexes will have to sell their Strategy shares. JPMorgan earlier estimated that selling at about $2.8 billion. Strategy says the funds hold about 13 million shares, 3.1% of its stock. Its shares are down 1.8% before the open.

For Bitcoin news, that matters beyond one stock. Strategy is the steadiest corporate buyer of Bitcoin. Fewer index buyers for its shares could make it harder and more costly to raise money for new purchases.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

The ETF selling started before either shock. To see how big the ETF side of this Bitcoin news is, we added up the daily net flows of the U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs for every trading day in November.

The streak is not a record yet. The longest run of outflows this year lasted 13 trading days in May and June, just before Bitcoin fell below $60,000.

The Fed adds to the pressure. October’s hot inflation report on Tuesday pushed the odds of a December rate hike on Polymarket to about 97%. Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more, which tends to pull money out of funds like these.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, it sits below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight. The 50-day EMA stands at $78,696 and the 200-day EMA at $76,422.

The next Bitcoin news to watch is Thursday’s ETF flow data and how Nvidia trades at the open. A sixth day of outflows and a weak tech session would put $72,727 to the test.

#5236. Kevin O'Leary Reveals What's Really Behind Crypto Market Crash

Renowned investor and Shark Tank personality Kevin O’Leary has shared his thoughts on the current cryptocurrency crash, stating that the crypto industry faces issues that extend far beyond Bitcoin's dropping price.

In particular, Mr. Wonderful, as O'Leary is better known, believes that one of the biggest issues the crypto industry faces is the lack of regulatory clarity in the United States. This prevents big financial firms from adopting blockchain and stablecoin technologies.

According to O'Leary, institutional crypto adoption has slowed to a crawl. Companies are unwilling to invest any capital until there is clarity around regulations.

"It's not just about Bitcoin in the crypto sell-off. The adoption of stablecoins and blockchain within institutions has slowed down. Companies are waiting for clarity on regulations," O'Leary wrote.

The billionaire investor shared that his company already utilizes Circle's USDC for treasury management and international settlements. However, many other companies are afraid to follow suit since their compliance teams aren't sure about the regulatory landscape.

"We use USDC for treasury management and cross-border settlement. But many others won't do it till their compliance guys know the rules," O'Leary added.

The famous investor focused on two major U.S. bills regarding cryptocurrency: the GENIUS Act and the CLARITY Act.

"We got the GENIUS Act going. We need the CLARITY Act for the rest," Kevin O'Leary concluded.

O'Leary has long raised concerns about the crypto space and the reasons why Bitcoin is not seeing more institutional investment yet.

For example, on Oct. 28, the billionaire investor named two main issues affecting Bitcoin. The first was regulatory uncertainty, and the second was the rising threat of quantum computing.

#5235. ‘I Signed Up for a Marathon at the Worst Possible Time—And It Was the Best Decision I Made’

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

“If you wait until you feel ready, you’ll be waiting forever.”

I wasn’t planning on running a marathon this year, let alone the New York City Marathon. Between its notoriously hilly course, relentless bridges, and the logistics of traveling across the country from my home in Colorado, NYC wasn’t exactly the easiest to take on. I’m also a busy mama to a 3½-year-old and 2-year-old, I work full time (I am the founding coach of the Ladder app and coach Team Body and Bell), and I had sinus surgery about six months ago. A marathon definitely wasn’t on my bingo card among the trenches of motherhood—but it happened.

After a really healthy and injury-free training block, I made it to the starting line. It was time for me to have my redemptive victory, but instead, I rolled up with the flu. At the time, I had no idea, and I chalked up how lousy I was feeling to the exhaustion of traveling with two little kids, lack of sleep, and all the chaos that comes with it. It wasn’t until I got home and was diagnosed that I realized what I’d actually been dealing with on race day. From the starting line, I found myself self-loathing and robbed of the marathon experience I’d worked so hard for.

But little did I know, the setbacks and imperfections of race day and training were actually going to allow me to experience the marathon even more than if I had been chasing a pace and finish time.

Between two pregnancies and postpartum periods, a C-section, and other unplanned health setbacks, it had been a difficult few years. I felt constantly defeated. Even as someone who works in fitness, I felt like I hadn’t done much to take care of myself in quite some time.

When the marathon opportunity presented itself, there was something almost rebellious about being able to choose my own hard in spite of the daily challenges that were out of my control as a mom.

As I was flooded with mom guilt, I kept asking myself: When will it be a good time to do this? When is it a good time to do anything for yourself as a mom? The answer was a resounding never. So I decided to rip off the bandaid, find a bib (thank you, Gatorade!), and fully commit to a three-month training block with a coach. (I hired a Body and Bell member who had actually trained with me since the start of the app. She is a seven-time NYC Marathoner and the most passionate running coach I know. Check her out on Instagram: @lindaleighlore.)

My life did not stop during this time. Work was more demanding than ever. We went on two family vacations. The kids got me sick multiple times. The training conditions were never perfect—but I did manage to get the mileage in. I reminded myself of something I say as a coach all the time: “It doesn’t need to be perfect, it just needs to be done.”

Let me preface something important as someone who works in fitness: endurance training was very new to me. I am a speed, power, and strength girlie at heart. The three-hour-plus long runs, pounding the pavement and moving slower, was very mentally unstimulating and out of my comfort zone.

But this new sport allowed me to enter a headspace I had never experienced before. There was something so recharging about being able to leave the house, put my phone in my pocket, and be in my own thoughts that healed me in ways I didn’t know I needed to be healed. Training did not only provide a break from the kids, but it also gave me a space to allow me to become more available for them.

In the fitness world, running and strength training are often viewed as two completely different styles of training. We have strength versus cardio zealots. But what more people need to understand is how much they thrive together.

The aerobic engine I was building with running gave me more cardio capacity for my lifts (lifting heavier felt smoother than it ever had) and all the muscle I had gained over the years made me an extremely strong and resilient runner (I recovered so well in between runs).

I felt structurally and aerobically unstoppable.

When I got to the start line, I knew something was off. I grew up as an athlete and knew what to expect with the competition nerves—but this was different. I was coughing, had a sore throat, and a raging headache. I kept telling myself it would all go away once I started moving. And for a while, it did. But around mile six, somewhere deep in Brooklyn, the symptoms came back with a vengeance, along with full-body chills.

It was way too early to be “bonking” in a marathon, and I was confused and simply annoyed. I tried to stay toward the middle of the street, away from the crowds. I purposely didn’t wear headphones to take in the crowd’s energy, yet there I was, trying to hide from it.

I crossed the Queensboro Bridge into Manhattan, where I knew my family was waiting for me at mile 17. I was so excited to see them, but I was also dragging so badly by this point, and I needed to take a quick break. I quickly took some medicine, gave some hugs, and kept trekking on.

I knew the only way out was through. I focused on one mile at a time, kept taking my gel, and tried to stay positive. Thankfully, that's the beautiful thing about a major marathon: There are reasons all around you to keep pushing. Everywhere I turned, I saw people of all ages, backgrounds, and abilities, with their own reasons for being out there. It was impossible not to feel inspired—or reminded that I was part of something so much bigger than my own race.It wasn’t until mile 22, shockingly on the Fifth Avenue climb to Central Park, where I had a breakthrough that felt supernatural—a combo of adrenaline and gratitude for what my body was doing. I was able to see my family one last time and then finish the race strong.

I was expecting to cross the finish line feeling so victorious, maybe even relieved that it was over. But I felt kind of disappointed. Not because of how I’d performed, but because this thing I’d spent months training for, thinking about, and looking forward to was suddenly over.

So let me be the first to tell you that what you get out of a marathon has very little to do with how fast you finish. And that's not to take anything away from people who work incredibly hard to get faster and faster in this sport. That's amazing! But the marathon is the great equalizer, and here's what I mean.

The marathon is hard for everyone. It doesn’t matter how fast you run it or whether it’s your first marathon or your 10th. There's a camaraderie that develops on the course because everyone is going through something so taxing together. You're all hurting, you're all pushing through, and your pace doesn't change that.

Plus, no two marathons are the same: different climates, crowds, elevations, and race-day challenges (like getting sick!). Your finish time cannot possibly capture everything you experienced out there. And it certainly doesn't always reflect the months of hard work you put into training or what you're actually capable of.

Then there's the sheer physical demand of the distance. A marathon requires so much time on your feet. You have to have a fueling strategy (salt…hydration…carbs…). No matter your pace, 26.2 miles is going to take it all out of you.

But maybe the most incredible part is that everyone out there is running for a different reason. You will see people out there of all ages, with limb differences, on wheels, with vision impairments, pregnant, pausing mid-race to breastfeed, after a weight-loss transformation. You name it. Everyone has a story, which makes the marathon one of the most inspiring environments you get to run in.

Bandit Running Women's Vanisher™ V-Neck Race Crop

My point with all of this: If you wait until you feel ready, you’ll be waiting forever.

If you want to get better at running, dabble in a 5K or 10K, or even a half-marathon. But if you want to learn who you really are deep within your core, sign up for the marathon. There's something about those 26.2 miles that shows you a side of yourself you might never have met otherwise. But you have to surrender to every mile and let the race have its way with you to truly transform.

And if you’re a busy mama like me—debating if you can, debating if it’s fair to the kids, debating if it’s the right time—there is no right time. There will always be a sick kid, a work deadline, a setback, a reason to wait. You aren’t promised to show up to the start line feeling your best.

Not because you have anything to prove. You get through bedtime every night without a crowd cheering you on or a medal waiting at the finish line. You're already doing hard things every single day. But sometimes you need to choose something hard just for you to remember what you're capable of.

And maybe the best part isn't even what you discover about yourself along the way. It's that your kids get to grow up watching their mom go after something she wants, even when the timing isn't perfect, even when it's hard, and even when it would be so much easier not to.

Lauren Kanski, CPT, is a member of the Women’s Health advisory board, a NASM-certified personal trainer, and a kettlebell and strength training specialist. She is the founding coach of the Ladder fitness app, where she leads Team Body and Bell, a strength training program focused on building muscle, power, and confidence. She lives in Colorado with her husband and two little ones.
